text:
Marathon Petroleum rose 2.0% today as oil refineries operated at exceptionally high capacity (96.8%), supporting strong margins for processors like MPC. The gain caps a remarkable two-week run of nearly 9%, driven by tight supply conditions—US oil at $107/barrel and global oil at $130.80/barrel—that boost the value of refined products like gasoline and diesel. Refineries running near full tilt while inventories of gasoline and diesel remain relatively modest create favorable conditions for refiner profitability.

The broader backdrop includes geopolitical uncertainty around Middle Eastern oil that had pushed prices higher, though today's news of Saudi Arabia offering additional crude supplies via the Strait of Hormuz actually eased some supply-disruption fears. That said, the record diesel prices cited in today's coverage and the persistent gap between US and global oil prices suggest the refining environment remains supportive for a company converting crude into fuel.
